The logic clip is a simple test instrument used to determine logic levels on an IC. The clip is attached to an IC where it makes contact with each pin. On the logic clip are LEDs or lamps, one for each pin connection to the IC.
Again, the signature analyzer is only used in very complex circuits where the cost of the instrument can be justified.

The instrument converts a series of ones and zeros at a given test point to hexadecimal code. The code is called the signature for that particular test point. Then, by comparing the signature to the known signature, you can identify faults...
Signature analyzers are used to locate faults to the component level in microprocessor based systems.
The signature analyzer is somewhat like the logic analyzer without the waveform display. It uses the coded format by measuring pulse trains of highs and lows.

Another type of format that may be included on some logic analyzers is the CODED format. The coded format changes ones and zeros to either octal or hexadecimal code.

The second type of format is the BIT or BIT PATTERN. A sequence of 1s and 0s from a functional circuit can be compared to the pattern of a faulty circuit to detect errors. Oscilloscopes and logic probes cannot do this...

One type of format is the TIMING DIAGRAM. Several pulse waveforms are displayed in the correct time relationship. Dual channel oscilloscopes can only display two waveforms. Logic analyzers can display many, depending on the make and model...

The logic analyzer is basically a special type of multichannel oscilloscope that has the ability to display logic levels, pulse trains of highs and lows, in several formats. Logic analyzers are expensive and only used in complex digital circuits.

The current tracer and logic pulser are used to find points in a digital circuit that are stuck, that is, the point remains a logic 1 or 0 all the time. It is particularly difficult to isolate a bad IC when several are connected together. The current tracer and logic pulser make the job easier...

The current tracer and logic pulser are very simple test instruments that measure pulsating current at a particular point in a circuit. Their appearance is very similar to the logic probe, and they are often used in conjunction with the logic probe...

A logic probe can indicate a high signal, a low signal, single pulse, multiple pulses or an open or bad level. Even though the logic probe is very useful for detecting faults quickly, it normally must be used with other types of digital test instruments to locate problems that are more than just a missing or incorrect input.....
The probe provides a simple means of measuring highs, lows and pulses. The probe is nothing more than one or more LEDs that illuminate for certain types of signal inputs.

The logic probe is the least expensive of all digital test instruments. It is especially designed to be used with digital circuits. Logic probes measure logic levels. Note, logic probes do not measure actual DC values.
Also, signals viewed by the oscilloscope must be periodic. In other words, they must repeat themselves in the same pattern over and over to be seen on the oscilloscope display properly.

The multiplexer allows up to 16 signals to be viewed on the oscilloscope simultaneously. If you try to check the output of a data bus, you can see where being able to look at all the lines can be important...

However, oscilloscopes have one disadvantage when used in microprocessor systems. Only one or two waveforms can usually be displayed at one time. This disadvantage is overcome by using an oscilloscope multiplexer....
One of the big advantages of using a dual trace oscilloscope is that two waveforms can be measured at the same time. In this way, the time relationship can be determined and analyzed.
An oscilloscope can also be used to measure logic highs and lows which are DC values. In addition, pulse waveforms and square waves can be measured.
Characteristics such as amplitude, rise and fall times, pulse width, and frequency can be quickly determined from oscilloscope measurements..ments.
In digital circuits, the oscilloscope is one of the most versatile instruments. The oscilloscope can detect abnormalities in waveforms that other instruments cannot.
The oscilloscope provides a visual display of a voltage waveform and measures AC and DC voltages and period. frequency, and phase.
The oscilloscope is a lot more expensive than the multimeter; however, there are not many electronic repair shops that do not have at least one...

But, if the levels are changing, or these are pulsed inputs or outputs, the multimeter is of little use. Since there are other means to measure operating voltages and logic levels, the multimeter is not used very often, only for continuity checks or pins that maintain static voltage levels, like Vcc or ground...
Many have different ranges of values that represent high and low conditions. As long as the logic levels are constant, a multimeter will give an accurate reading of HIGH or LOW.

Logic highs and lows may also be measured using a multimeter. A high is normally between 2 and 12 VDC while a low is between 0 and 2 VDC. Remember, you must have knowledge about the IC family you are using...
PC card wires are checked by measuring continuity between points on the card. Continuity indicates a good connection; no continuity indicates an open wire.

The trend in digital electronics is to use the lowest Vcc values that the chips can be made to run on. This helps reduce heat problems. Many circuits in development today are designed to run all the way down below 1 volt to represent a high condition...

In digital electronics, multimeters are used primarily to measure operating power, that is Vcc, and checking for open or shorted wires on printed circuit cards. Vcc is normally a DC voltage between 1 and 12 volts...
Multimeters measure DC and AC voltages, DC and AC current and resistances. Some even test transistors, diodes and capacitors.
The multimeter is the most commonly used test instrument in DC and AC circuits. However, it is not the most commonly used test instrument in digital circuits....
Because of these differences, several special types of digital test instruments have been developed. Let's begin the discussion on digital test equipment with the multimeter and the oscilloscope...
The testing of digital circuitry is different from analog circuitry in several ways.
* Digital Circuits use Low DC Voltages. 0, 1.3, 3, 5 and 12 VDC
are the most common voltages encountered.
* Digital Circuits normally do not have AC voltages present.
* Digital Circuits do not normally require resistance checks
* Digital Circuits often rely on timing. That is, synchronization
between signals is vital for proper operation.
* Digital Circuits use IC's. Since IC's can not be repaired,

In this course you have possibly used a multimeter, oscilloscope and logic probe depending on the equipment that you used in the experiments. However, you should know what other types of test equipment are available to you...
In digital electronics, the oscilloscope and multimeter are used, along with several other types of test instruments.

In DC circuits, the multimeter is the best choice for measuring circuit values of voltage, current and resistance. In AC circuits, the oscilloscope is invaluable for determining the characteristics of waveforms...
In each area of electronics, different types of test equipment provide the best means for circuit measurements. Digital electronics is no exception.
In your studies of electronics, you have learned that multimeters and oscilloscopes are invaluable in determining correct circuit operation and for troubleshooting faulted circuits.
In the experiment you will have the opportunity to use some of the test equipment discussed.

However, it is just as important to know how to use other tools which can speed up the troubleshooting process. This section of the lesson is not going to teach you how to use the most common troubleshooting tools, but it will introduce them to you...
A computer repair technician must select tools which are appropriate to the troubleshooting task. Often you will choose tools that you are familiar with..
Heat buildup may cause components to fail. Dust, dirt and other airborne particles can also conduct electricity which can cause arcing and shorts.

Another preventive maintenance action is routine cleaning. Dust tends to stick to a printed circuit board. When a printed circuit board gets coated by a layer of dust, the dust becomes an insulator and holds in the heat...
So, at a convenient time, you re-adjust the power supply. What you did was preventive maintenance: you found a situation that may cause a failure later on and fixed it.

However, you decide to measure the output voltages of the power supply. The measurements show that the +5V to each chip is measuring +8V. Even though the system operates correctly, the output voltage may eventually damage some of the chips in the microprocessor system...

As the name implies, this maintenance is accomplished before the system has a chance to fail. For example, suppose that your microprocessor is operating correctly and there are no signs of system failure...

For a technician, troubleshooting is unavoidable, but the frequency of equipment failure can be dramatically reduced by eliminating potential problems before they begin. This is accomplished by a process called Preventive Maintenance...

Most technicians, after practice, can insert and remove an IC by hand or with a screwdriver. However, IC insertion and removal tools are manufactured and should be used whenever possible. These tools make insertion and removal simple, and greatly reduce the risk of damaging an IC...

To remove an IC, lift up, being careful not to bend any pins. This will require a rocking motion. Ensure that one end of the IC is not completely removed before the other end because this will bend pins...

To insert the IC, line up all its legs with the socket connectors and then press it down gently. Ensure all legs have begun to slide into their appropriate socket locations before pushing the IC in the rest of the way...
Pin 1 of the IC should be inserted as shown below. Remember, inserting a chip backwards can destroy the chip when power is applied.

Before trying to insert an IC, check that its legs are straight and evenly spaced. ICs have a dimple, dot or notch used for orientation. The pins are numbered starting at 1 and go counterclockwise from the orientation mark...
Because of this, most ICs are now placed in sockets with the sockets soldered to the PC board before the IC is inserted. In this way, IC chips can avoid heat-related damage.
Installing ICs requires special attention and sometimes special equipment. Soldering an IC, especially a CMOS chip, can destroy the device no matter how careful you are.

The only sure method to determine the type of IC is to use the manufacturer's data books. Many manufacturers include a date mark on the chip. This date usually indicates the month and year the chip was made. The date helps identify the chip, especially if the manufacturer changes the method used to identify the chip. Other types of marking may include: * Manufacturer's part number * Inspection Markings * Source of Supply * Manufacturing locationnn

Identification codes usually consist of three parts: a prefix number, a device number, and a suffix. However, each manufacturer uses a different type of code which, in most cases, is similar to this...

The only way you can be sure that the replacement IC is the same, is to check the specifications for both chips. This requires knowing the manufacturer. Many data books provide a cross-reference for direct replacement of an IC built by a different manufacturer..
Chip specifications can be looked up in the manufacturer's data books. This information is very important when replacing an IC with one from a different manufacturer.

IC identification codes vary depending on the manufacturer. Manufacturer recognition is important when replacing chips and researching IC data. Microprocessor systems use many integrated circuits. These ICs look similar except for the number of pins and the labeling on the cases. Pin number identification and proper IC placement are extremely important...
SOCKETS: Check that IC's are seated in their proper sockets
properly, not tilted. When soldering sockets in place, solder
diagonally opposite pins from the farthest corners first and
check to see that the socket is flat against the circuit board.
Then the remaining pins can be easily soldered into place.
SWITCHES: Don't use solvents to clean switches and don't use
a pencil to switch rocker switches. If substances get between
the switch contacts, its operation may become impaired.

Operating the system in the proper environment will help to prevent time consuming and expensive repairs in the future.
There are certain environmental limitations in which a microprocessor system can be stored and operated:
1. The system should not be stored in a dusty environment.
2. The system should only be operated within the manufacturer's specified temperature limitations.
3. The system should always be plugged into a grounded outlet.
4. The system must not be operated near an unshielded power supply of other equipment. Strong emissions from power supplies can force crystals to vibrate at the wrong frequency.

Once you are sure that you know about the microprocessor you are working on, then, and only then, should you begin troubleshooting.
Before troubleshooting, think about the sections of the microprocessor and what role they play in the system operation.

1. Which components are not necessary for successful execution of an interaction with the monitor program? Disconnecting all nonessential assemblies may make the machine operational again. In this case, you can deduce that the fault is in one of the disconnected devices, or the interfacing signals.
2. How can you check that the system is starting correctly when the power is applied? Which components are essential in starting the system?
3. How can you test that the keypad and the display are working correctly?
4. How can you test that the other peripheral devices are working correctly?
A fault in an essential function may be minor enough not to affect the basic system operations yet be responsible for a less noticeable fault.

In this case, the technician may choose to begin investigating the suspect area without going through checks of the more essential system functions. As a novice technician, you should be as thorough as possible in your observation of the essential functions...

Occasionally, the fault may allow most of the microprocessor functions to work properly. The symptoms may be specific enough to assure the experienced technician that the essential functions are working, and also allow the technician to deduce which area is causing the problem...
You must check the symptoms for yourself before probing into the microprocessor for the cause of these symptoms.

Even if the user does supply a description of the fault symptoms, remember that the user is probably looking at it without the proper electronics knowledge to actually know what they are seeing wrong...

Much time can be wasted if the technician jumps to conclusions without sufficient evidence. In most cases, you will be given equipment to troubleshoot with little information on the history of that particular piece of equipment...

It is equally important for a technician to be methodical when troubleshooting. The technician must always keep sight of the overall troubleshooting task and yet, at the same time, be attentive to details...
In order to troubleshoot, a technician must have an adequate understanding of both the equipment under test and the test equipment being used. However, this alone does not make a good technician...
